The v2 JSON API requires token authentication for access; authentication is not treated as a grant of proprietary rights. Only exact target-name and bounded date results from the documented photometry endpoint are eligible.

Only public ADS bibliographic metadata is retained. CTAS does not download, mirror, or assert reuse rights for article full text; publisher and repository links retain their own access and reuse terms. Event association requires an exact retained transient name.

The adapter uses ESO's anonymous TAP service only and retains a reduced-product row only when obs_release_date is present and no later than the query time. ESO states that the proprietary period protects raw and derived data until release and distributes archive data under CC BY 4.0 with acknowledgment requirements. No product bytes are downloaded.

Gaia DR3 is a public ESA data release and ESA identifies CDS as an official Gaia partner data centre. This anonymous adapter is allowlisted to the VizieR copy of catalogue I/355/gaiadr3, stores catalog rows and provider links only, and does not query unrelated VizieR collections or retrieve DataLink products.
Each retained row passed a mission-specific past-release check; XMM also required data_in_heasarc=Y and NICER required VALIDATED. No file bytes were downloaded.

The adapter is anonymous and restricted to the provider-documented public AllWISE Source Catalog and 2MASS Point Source Catalog. It stores catalog rows and official links only; proprietary/exclusive-access IRSA holdings are outside the allowlist.
Only observation and product rows explicitly marked PUBLIC are retained. Product bytes remain provider-hosted; this system stores metadata and official download links only.

The anonymous public NED TAP service documents programmatic cone searches of the NED Object Directory and requests NED acknowledgment. CTAS retains bounded source-native rows and provenance only. NED states that high-volume automated access is best-effort, so this adapter is single-threaded, starts at most one request per second, and never queries proprietary or user-account holdings.

NOIRLab's provider-owned API authentication notebook states that anyone may retrieve public files while proprietary-file retrieval requires authorization. This adapter sends no credential and retains a product only after an exact file-metadata lookup supplies a nonblank release_date no later than the query time. Anonymous metadata about unreleased files is counted only for exclusion and is never stored. Product bytes are not downloaded.

Rubin alert packets are world-public with no proprietary period, and Fink documents its LSST Science Portal and REST API as real-time, public services requiring no login. Coordinate and first-detection proximity are not proof of source identity.

SIMBAD documents free access without registration under the ODbL license. This adapter uses the anonymous official TAP service for one bounded coordinate query, retains provider attribution and source bibcodes, and does not treat a nearby literature object as the transient, its host, or a new detection.

The official TNS 2.0 API manual documents an object-level public field and a per-spectrum public field. Only an object explicitly marked public=1 and spectrum rows explicitly marked public=1 are normalized. Photometry rows are refused because the current response does not supply a per-row public/private marker.

WISeREP's official help states that private data require a personal API key for scripted access. CTAS sends no credentials, requests public=yes explicitly, and accepts only rows independently marked public=1 from the anonymous public export.

A zero result means ALeRCE holds no public ZTF alert object at this position in the window; it is not a forced-photometry nondetection. Public ZTF alert photometry served by the ALeRCE broker. Cite Förster et al. (2021), AJ 161, 242, and acknowledge ALeRCE and the Zwicky Transient Facility according to current provider guidance.
A zero result may reflect public-release latency or catalog non-detection; it is not a forced-photometry nondetection.

rules.classification: Spectroscopic classes and alert or messenger labels are different definitions and are not compared; two active classes differ when neither label refines the other (for example 'SN Ia' and 'SN Ia-91T' agree); an earlier value from the same provider is a revision.
rules.host: Two proposed hosts agree when their names match after case and spacing are ignored or one name is among the other's NED cross-identifications; otherwise they are an identity ambiguity. Association probabilities are not computed.
rules.photometry: Only exactly compatible photometry (same epoch, band, system, method, calibration and direct/difference state, two or more providers) is compared. The limiting magnitude or flux that a provider reports alongside a detection is that epoch's detection threshold, not a non-detection, and is not compared with the detection; a detection brighter than another provider's non-detection limit at the same epoch is a status conflict. A group is listed only when it is still inconsistent under these rules; at most 10 groups per event, most significant first.
rules.position: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.
rules.redshift: Two redshifts with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 0.005 (about 1,500 km/s); transient and host redshifts are different definitions and are listed, not compared; host redshifts of differently named hosts are an identity ambiguity.
rules.revision: A retracted row, or a superseded row of the same provider whose value differs beyond the property's rule, is a revision or retraction; a revision within the rule is consistent; the earlier value stays visible.
rules.sigma: Two values that both state an uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 3 combined standard deviations (uncertainties added in quadrature; a stated position error radius is treated as one standard deviation).

rules.classification: Spectroscopic classes and alert or messenger labels are different definitions and are not compared; two active classes differ when neither label refines the other (for example 'SN Ia' and 'SN Ia-91T' agree); an earlier value from the same provider is a revision.
rules.host: Two proposed hosts agree when their names match after case and spacing are ignored or one name is among the other's NED cross-identifications; otherwise they are an identity ambiguity. Association probabilities are not computed.
rules.photometry: Only exactly compatible photometry (same epoch, band, system, method, calibration and direct/difference state, two or more providers) is compared. The limiting magnitude or flux that a provider reports alongside a detection is that epoch's detection threshold, not a non-detection, and is not compared with the detection; a detection brighter than another provider's non-detection limit at the same epoch is a status conflict. A group is listed only when it is still inconsistent under these rules; at most 10 groups per event, most significant first.
rules.position: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.
rules.redshift: Two redshifts with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 0.005 (about 1,500 km/s); transient and host redshifts are different definitions and are listed, not compared; host redshifts of differently named hosts are an identity ambiguity.
rules.revision: A retracted row, or a superseded row of the same provider whose value differs beyond the property's rule, is a revision or retraction; a revision within the rule is consistent; the earlier value stays visible.
rules.sigma: Two values that both state an uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 3 combined standard deviations (uncertainties added in quadrature; a stated position error radius is treated as one standard deviation).

evidence_timeline.summary: Public Rubin diaObject inside the target cone and discovery-window query. This is a positional association candidate only: CTAS has not added a Rubin alias, merged identities, or imported its history.

We compile public optical photometry for the Type Ic-BL supernova SN 2026acxa. The ZTF i-band non-detection on MJD 61303.1 reaches 19.36 mag, corresponding to an absolute magnitude limit of roughly -13.35. Given the 5-day cadence gap and the rapid rise to peak, we estimate a discovery lag of approximately 2 to 4 days. AstroNote 2026-314 reported a near-infrared excess modeled with a blackbody radius of about 6e15 cm. By estimating the expected ejecta expansion using typical velocities, we find the ejecta would only reach about 5.5e15 cm in 40 days. This kinematic mismatch supports the pre-existing circumstellar dust echo interpretation. We encourage rapid near-infrared spectroscopic follow-up.
evidence_timeline.title: Pre-explosion Constraints and Circumstellar Dust Geometry of the Type Ic-BL SN 2026acxa

evidence_timeline.summary: We report J+Hs-band photometry of the nearby Type Ic-BL supernova SN 2026acxa, with the MDM InfraRed Astronomy InGaAs Experiment (MIRAGE) instrument on the MDM 1.3-m telescope. Our recent photometry indicates that the source has exhibited a sustained reddening of from J - Hs = 0.02 (+2 days after explosion) to J - Hs = 0.63 Vega mag (+39 days), and is redder than SN 1998bw and normal SNe Ic at a similar phase, suggesting an emerging near-IR excess. We encourage continued multi-wavelength follow-up observations, particularly IR spectroscopy to characterize the possible dust emission.
evidence_timeline.title: Discovery of an emerging near-IR excess in the nearby Type Ic-BL SN 2026acxa with MDM/MIRAGE

publication_revisions.abstract: We compile public optical photometry for the Type Ic-BL supernova SN 2026acxa. The ZTF i-band non-detection on MJD 61303.1 reaches 19.36 mag, corresponding to an absolute magnitude limit of roughly -13.35. Given the 5-day cadence gap and the rapid rise to peak, we estimate a discovery lag of approximately 2 to 4 days. AstroNote 2026-314 reported a near-infrared excess modeled with a blackbody radius of about 6e15 cm. By estimating the expected ejecta expansion using typical velocities, we find the ejecta would only reach about 5.5e15 cm in 40 days. This kinematic mismatch supports the pre-existing circumstellar dust echo interpretation. We encourage rapid near-infrared spectroscopic follow-up.
publication_revisions.authors_text: Chenhao Tang(China Amateur Sky Survey Network）
publication_revisions.title: Pre-explosion Constraints and Circumstellar Dust Geometry of the Type Ic-BL SN 2026acxa

publication_revisions.abstract: We report J+Hs-band photometry of the nearby Type Ic-BL supernova SN 2026acxa, with the MDM InfraRed Astronomy InGaAs Experiment (MIRAGE) instrument on the MDM 1.3-m telescope. Our recent photometry indicates that the source has exhibited a sustained reddening of from J - Hs = 0.02 (+2 days after explosion) to J - Hs = 0.63 Vega mag (+39 days), and is redder than SN 1998bw and normal SNe Ic at a similar phase, suggesting an emerging near-IR excess. We encourage continued multi-wavelength follow-up observations, particularly IR spectroscopy to characterize the possible dust emission.

persistedQueryReceipts.scope: The anonymous AVSpec search interface explicitly searches published observations. Only rows returned by that interface and anonymously downloadable from the matching official record identifier are eligible. AAVSO states that its hosted data may be used in publications when the current Data Usage Guidelines are followed.

AAVSO states that International Database observations are freely available to the community for research and publication subject to its current Data Usage Guidelines. The v2 JSON API requires token authentication for access; authentication is not treated as a grant of proprietary rights. Only exact target-name and bounded date results from the documented photometry endpoint are eligible.

Only public ADS bibliographic metadata is retained. CTAS does not download, mirror, or assert reuse rights for article full text; publisher and repository links retain their own access and reuse terms. Event association requires an exact retained transient name.

The adapter uses ESO's anonymous TAP service only and retains a reduced-product row only when obs_release_date is present and no later than the query time. ESO states that the proprietary period protects raw and derived data until release and distributes archive data under CC BY 4.0 with acknowledgment requirements. No product bytes are downloaded.
Each retained row passed a mission-specific past-release check; XMM also required data_in_heasarc=Y and NICER required VALIDATED. No file bytes were downloaded.
Only observation and product rows explicitly marked PUBLIC are retained. Product bytes remain provider-hosted; this system stores metadata and official download links only.

Rubin alert packets are world-public with no proprietary period, and Fink documents its LSST Science Portal and REST API as real-time, public services requiring no login. Coordinate and first-detection proximity are not proof of source identity.
No unvalidated, non-public, or ambiguous scientific record was stored.

WISeREP's official help states that private data require a personal API key for scripted access. CTAS sends no credentials, requests public=yes explicitly, and accepts only rows independently marked public=1 from the anonymous public export.

A zero result means ALeRCE holds no public ZTF alert object at this position in the window; it is not a forced-photometry nondetection. Public ZTF alert photometry served by the ALeRCE broker. Cite Förster et al. (2021), AJ 161, 242, and acknowledge ALeRCE and the Zwicky Transient Facility according to current provider guidance.

These are released catalog measurements, not alert difference photometry and not forced photometry. Coordinate association does not assert identity. Public ZTF data-release light curves served by NASA/IPAC IRSA. Cite the ZTF survey/data-release papers and acknowledge IRSA according to current guidance.
